newsitem.title: USA: White House says may delay FY 98 budget proposal.
newsitem.headline: White House says may delay FY 98 budget proposal.

text.p: White House spokesman Mike McCurry said Monday the Clinton administration is considering delaying the submission of its fiscal year 1998 budget proposal slightly beyond its expected release on February 3.

McCurry told reporters one possibility under discussion was to delay the budget until after President Bill Clinton's annual state of the union address, which is expected on February 5. He said one date that had been discussed for the budget was February 7, but said no decision had been made.
He also said that Clinton had made most of the major decisions needed to prepare the fiscal 1998 budget.

"It would technically be due (February) the third, but because we're doing the state of the union the fifth, there is some discussion of doing the budget later that week rather than at the beginning of the week," McCurry said.

Asked if the date of February 7 had been discussed, McCurry said: "There have been some discussions about that but I don't know that that's been formalized yet. The last I heard this morning, we were still having discussions with Congress about it."

"He's made most of the major decisions necessary for the budget," McCurry added. "There are a couple of items, some significant items, that are still under discussion as to the shape although I think that the general direction of how we're coming out on that is known to those who are doing the work."
McCurry said the FY 1998 budget would be broadly similar to Clinton's previous submissions, but gave no details.

"The premise of our budget is going to be very much like that that you've heard in the past," McCurry said. "The general, broad philosophical construct of the budget will be similar ... there are some difference of nuances."
